name: Gnome
summary: Gnomes in Ironforge fight to reclaim Gnomeregan, their poisoned home. Across Azeroth, they are renowned for engineering and arcane mastery, and remain staunch allies even in exile.

sections.title: Ingenuity and Optimism
sections.body: Gnomes are small in stature and vast in intellect. Curiosity drives them to study machines and magic, and to invent what no one has built before. Clockwork devices, flying machines, and subterranean trains are among their works. Hardship has not dimmed their cheer; they still mean to rebuild and solve what seems impossible.

sections.title: Forged in the Mountains
sections.body: The gnomes made their home in the frozen crags of Dun Morogh. There, they found kinship with the dwarves of Ironforge. Together, dwarven strength and gnomish ingenuity carved Gnomeregan, a remarkable city beneath western Dun Morogh. Visionary leaders called High Tinkers lead the gnomes.

sections.title: The Fall of Gnomeregan
sections.body:
During the Third War, gnomes sent armaments to Lordaeron but held back their troops, leaving their allies confused. Savage troggs, stirred by excavations near Uldaman, had surged into Gnomeregan's lower sectors.

Hoping to drive them out without burdening an embattled Alliance, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque followed his chief advisor's counsel and vented radioactive waste into the lower city. The plan failed. The troggs survived, mutated and frenzied, while nearly eighty percent of the gnomish people perished.

sections.title: Exile in Tinker Town
sections.body:
The surviving gnomes fled their poisoned home and found sanctuary with their dwarven cousins in Ironforge. High Tinker Mekkatorque and his people made their home in Ironforge's Tinker Town. There, they continue to support the Alliance and oversee the Deeprun Tram to Stormwind.

From this adopted quarter, gnomish commandos and volunteers make repeated expeditions into Gnomeregan's irradiated depths. They seek to clear the troggs and mechanical abominations from their grand city and reclaim it someday.

faq.q: Why are gnomes living in Ironforge instead of their own city?
faq.answer: Gnomes live in Ironforge as refugees because subterranean troggs overran their ancestral home, Gnomeregan. A desperate plan to irradiate the troggs failed, filling the city with lethal fallout and killing most of its inhabitants. King Magni Bronzebeard offered the survivors shelter in the dwarven capital.

High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque leads the gnomes. They choose leaders for merit, engineering skill, and visionary thinking rather than a hereditary royal line. Mekkatorque ordered Gnomeregan irradiated to stop the troggs, and now directs the effort to reclaim their home.

faq.q: Why didn't the gnomes help fight the Scourge in Lordaeron?
faq.answer: The gnomes sent siege weapons and technology to the Alliance of Lordaeron, but Gnomeregan was fighting for survival against troggs, so they could not spare soldiers. They did not ask their allies for help, believing the Alliance had enough to face the undead Scourge.

The Deeprun Tram is a subterranean railway designed by High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and built by gnomish engineers. It links Tinker Town in Ironforge directly to the dwarven district of Stormwind City, letting troops, supplies, and travelers move rapidly between the allied capitals.

faq.q: What is the rivalry between gnomes and goblins?
faq.answer: Gnomes and goblins have an intense cultural and technological rivalry that flared during the Second War. Gnomish engineering favors precision, stability, and intricate, safe mechanisms. Goblin engineering favors raw explosive power, cheap production, and swift results despite volatility. Both peoples try to out-invent and mock one another.
Gnomes train as warriors, rogues, priests, mages, and warlocks.

angles.text: As a gnome, you carry the loss of Gnomeregan with quiet resolve. From exile in Tinker Town, your brilliance, optimism, and explosive firepower help you fight for your stolen home.

As a dwarf, you have shared the mountains with the gnomes for generations; they are your oldest and dearest neighbors. Giving their survivors a home in Tinker Town was an easy choice for your people, bound to them by generations of brotherhood.

As an engineer, you know gnomish engineering across the world for its sophisticated contraptions, ray devices, and mind-boggling precision. Its meticulous designs differ from volatile goblin detonations.
As a mage, you share your people's gift for the arcane. Gnomes are exceptionally gifted arcanists despite their small stature.
As an Alliance member, you rely on gnomes for strategic mobility and siege technology. They faithfully supply machines and maintain the Deeprun Tram, even while displaced from their home.
